layer_1_no_defence.note: Baseline: with no defence every attack is delivered verbatim to the model.

layer_2_detection.note: Read these three rows in order. PLANTED is what the patterns were written against, so a high score there measures memorisation, not defence. PARAPHRASE was written blind and originally scored 2/8, which is the finding: keyword matching does not generalise. Class-level patterns were then added, taking it to 8/8 - but that figure is no longer blind. HELD_OUT was written afterwards and never tuned against, so it is the only honest generalisation number here, and it is the one to quote.

history.caveat: The 'after' figure is contaminated: the patterns were written to cover exactly these attack classes after seeing them fail.

layer_3_neutralisation.note: Structural: untrusted text is delimited and framed as data, and detected spans have their imperative force broken. Generalises beyond the patterns.

layer_2b_trained_classifier.note: A purpose-built injection classifier (Meta Prompt Guard 2), run on the same text as the pattern scanner. It is the control for the whole argument: if hand-written patterns failed merely because they were written badly, a model trained on this exact task should do better. Compare its held_out row against the pattern scanner's. Prompt Guard is trained on direct jailbreak attempts against a chat assistant; the held-out set is business-plausible social engineering inside a job post, which is a different thing entirely.

outcomes.detail: {'error': 'approval_required', 'detail': 'Submitting spends Connects. A human must approve it first.', 'irreversible': True}

layer_4_capability_denial.note: The decisive layer. Even an attack that defeats layers 2 and 3 cannot submit, because no analysis agent holds a write tool and the one that does refuses without a human approval token. Asserted by test, not sampled.

output_side_scan.note: Last check before a client sees anything: catches a successful injection.

residual_risk: A novel phrasing that no pattern matches and that reads as a legitimate client request will pass layers 2 and 3. Layer 4 is what makes that survivable.
An injection can still waste budget: it is read, analysed and flagged, and that costs tokens.
An injection that persuades the HUMAN - a plausible-looking request in the approval screen - is out of scope for these defences entirely.
